description:
backend.rs:260-265 — CalendarsBackend::calendar_has_events returns 'impl Future<Output = bool>'. No Result. A backend that has a transient storage failure has exactly two options:

1. Return false → handler proceeds to destroy_object, which itself can detect the storage failure and produce serverFail. BUT the calendarHasEvent guard is bypassed: if events DO exist but the read failed, the destroy proceeds, the events are silently orphaned (or destroy_object itself fails for a different reason), and the client sees inconsistent state.

2. Return true → silently blocks a legitimate destroy and the client gets a misleading calendarHasEvent error that hides a real transient backend issue.

Compare against the canonical jmap-mail-server (e.g. mail-server backend.rs:200-217, MailBackend::blob_exists) which uses Result<bool, Self::Error> with documented rationale: 'Returning Ok(false) for a transient backend failure is a bug: it surfaces as a deterministic-looking error and the client will not retry.'

This is a canonical-template divergence: the calendars-server signature was written without that lesson, so it now ships an API that cannot signal storage failure correctly. Same shape error as the original mail-server blob_exists shape before d87d482 widened it.

Fix: change to '-> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send'. Handler calendar.rs:252 maps Err to serverFail SetError on the destroy entry. This is an API break on CalendarsBackend, so it bundles with the next CallerCtx-class change window (the JMAP-g7wu pattern). It is not P0 because today every backend returns 'false' (the default in MemoryBackend at memory.rs:806-812 reads HashMap and can't fail), and the bool signature is consistent with no in-tree backend overriding it. Becomes urgent the first time a production backend wants to do an async DB query here.

Also: the doc comment on calendar_has_events (backend.rs:254-259) does NOT document the 'what does false really mean' question and does not warn implementors against silently swallowing errors. Whether or not the signature changes, this needs a 'must not silently swallow' paragraph.

P1 because the wrong signature on a freshly-shipped public trait method is the cookie-cutter-consistency regression that the canonical-template rule exists to catch BEFORE consumers depend on it.
title: calendar_has_events returns bool, swallows transient backend errors
